lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: survey, experiment, and observational study design
lessonRef.title: Independent application A: survey, experiment, and observational study design

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One reference example. Use it only if you get stuck.

items.prompt: n = 400, sample proportion 55%. Margin and interval?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: In 1000 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 44 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 4.4% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 4.4% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 55 and standard deviation 12. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 19 and 91?
choices: about 50%
about 95%
about 68%
about 99.7%

items.prompt: A researcher runs an observational study of volunteers who chose their own group. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.

items.prompt: A random sample of 400 people gives a sample proportion of 73%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±10%, giving 63% to 83%
±5%, giving 68% to 78%
±73%, giving 0% to 146%

items.prompt: In 500 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 3 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 0.6% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 0.6% of simulations, which is not unusual.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 106 and standard deviation 12. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 70 and 142?
choices: about 99.7%
about 50%
about 68%
about 95%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a sample survey with randomly selected participants. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.

items.prompt: A random sample of 100 people gives a sample proportion of 64%. Using the conservative margin of error 1/√n, give the approximate margin of error and the resulting interval.
choices: ±20%, giving 44% to 84%
±1%, giving 63% to 65%
±64%, giving 0% to 128%
±10%, giving 54% to 74%

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: In 100 simulations under the assumption of no difference, 2 produced a result at least as extreme as the one observed. What should be concluded?
choices: The simulation proves that the observed difference is real.
The observed result is statistically significant: it occurred in only 2% of simulations, below the usual 5% threshold.
The observed result is not statistically significant: it occurred in 2% of simulations, which is not unusual.
The simulation proves that there is no difference.

items.prompt: A quantity is approximately normal with mean 84 and standard deviation 9. Approximately what percentage of values lie between 66 and 102?
choices: about 95%
about 99.7%
about 68%
about 50%

items.prompt: A researcher runs a randomised controlled experiment with participants randomly assigned to treatments. What kind of conclusion does this design support?
choices: It supports generalising from the sample to the population, but not a causal claim.
It supports a causal conclusion about the treatment, within the population studied.
It supports both generalisation and causation, provided the sample is large.
It supports neither generalisation nor causation, because self-selection can bias both.
